list_entry.title: Most kinds of soil contain clay

A.explanation:
This conclusion is conditional. We want a conclusion that makes two Some claims. The premises did match:

Most pharmacies sell cosmetics. Most pharmacies sell shampoo or toothpaste.

But the conclusion would have needed to be “Some places that sell cosmetics also sell shampoo, and some places that sell cosmetics also sell toothpaste”.

B.explanation: This conclusion is a Most claim. We want a conclusion that makes two Some claims. The words “for, after all, since, because” (F.A.B.S.) directly indicate premises and indirectly indicate conclusions. Ideally, we don’t read any of this answer once we’ve already seen that the first claim was the conclusion and that the conclusion was a mismatch.

D.explanation:
This conclusion makes two Some claims, so it’s worth reading. The problem is that the first premise isn’t saying “Most P’s are S or T”, it’s saying “Most P’s that are S are also T”.

In the original argument, both Most claims were about the same group: “types of soil”. This answer would only match had the original argument said,

Most pharmacies that sell shampoo also sells toothpaste. Most sandy soil has organic material.

Consider the difference in meaning between these two claims:

Most people have an iPhone or an Android phone. vs. Most people that have an iPhone also have an Android phone.

E.explanation:
This has two Some claims in the conclusion, so it's worth reading.

Premise 1: Most pharmacies sell cosmetics. Premise 2: Most pharmacies sell shampoo or toothpaste.

Conclusion: Some cosmetics sell shampoo, and some cosmetics and toothpaste.
